title: Shapes
description:
The classic. Write a base class `Shape` and three derived classes, then two functions that work on **any** shape without knowing which kind it is.

`Shape`: virtual destructor, `virtual double area() const`, `virtual std::string name() const`. (Give the base versions any body, for example returning 0 and `"shape"`. The next-but-one lesson shows how to say "there is no sensible default".)

| Class | Constructor | Area | Name |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Circle` | `explicit Circle(double radius)` | 3.14159 × r² | `"circle"` |
| `Rectangle` | `Rectangle(double width, double height)` | w × h | `"rectangle"` |
| `Triangle` | `Triangle(double base, double height)` | b × h ÷ 2 | `"triangle"` |

Functions (the alias `Shapes` is provided):

- `double totalArea(const Shapes& shapes)`
- `std::string largestName(const Shapes& shapes)`: the `name()` of the shape with the biggest area, or `"none"` for an empty list.
hints: Each derived class overrides `area` and `name` with `override`. The base class needs `virtual ~Shape() = default;`.
The functions that work on any shape take `const Shape&` (or a container of `std::unique_ptr<Shape>`) and only call the virtual functions.
